failures.criterion: Acceptance 3: a sender can ask not to be kept, and the Legion daemon does, so Envoy and the daemon never both keep one message.
failures.evidence: It holds for this release and breaks across two, and nothing in the change records the release order. Measured live against one new listener (built from this head) with a Postgres-free rig under $TMPDIR: this branch's daemon publisher (packages/daemon/internal/notify.HTTPPublisher.Publish, built from this head and called exactly as the outbox calls it) got `listener returned 404 Not Found: {"error":"no holder for role t-daemon","reason":"unclaimed"}` and `errors.Is(err, notify.ErrNoHolder) = true`, and the kept lane held nothing for that role (`notifications.envoy.kept.role.t-daemon`: no message found). The previous release's publisher, built from this branch's base 80053e29c957, whose notify.go carries no Keep field, got `listener returned 202 Accepted: {... "kept":true,"kept_reason":"unclaimed"}` and `errors.Is(err, notify.ErrNoHolder) = false`, and `notifications.envoy.kept.role.t-daemon-old` then held that very message. So a deployment that releases the Envoy listener before the legion binary has both keepers at once: the daemon's outbox holds the row (the 202 is not ErrNoHolder, so the row takes neither the unheld path nor success) while Envoy also hands the message to the role's next holder. The Envoy listener and the legion binary are separate releases (`.github/workflows/release-envoy-listener.yaml`, `release.yaml`), so the order is a deployment choice nothing here constrains. No test in this tree can pin it, since it needs a binary of another release, and a test that read a workflow file would be the check-of-a-check the deployment instructions forbid; the remedy is one sentence of release order in the pull request body and in the envoy changelog fragment, or a listener-side change the architect chooses.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a kept message older than 1 hour when the role is claimed is not forwarded, and is dropped and counted.
proof.surface: The same live rig, on a test build whose keep window is shortened: a clone of this head at $TMPDIR with `const roleKeepWindow = 3 * time.Second` in place of `time.Hour` in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/role_keep.go, and nothing else changed. Stated here because an hour cannot be waited out: the age is the stream's own store time, which no caller chooses.
proof.observed: The publish was kept (202, event c486e2b2df1799731ed50a0252cf86f1); after 8 seconds the role was claimed; the holder was handed nothing for it; envoy_role_kept_expired_total moved 0 -> 1; the listener logged exactly `listener dropped a kept role message older than the keep window` with session_id ses_tester_rig, topic notifications.role.t-stale, delivery_status expired, role t-stale, age 8.05392618s.
proof.negativeControl: The same run's three messages kept inside the shortened window, claimed at once: all three were forwarded, in order, exactly once. So the drop is the age and not the build: the same binary forwards what is young and drops what is old.
